newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vatican delegation seeks news on Vietnam posts.
newsitem.headline: Vatican delegation seeks news on Vietnam posts.

text.p: A high-level Vatican delegation in Vietnam for talks with members of the country's communist government is seeking progress in troubled relations between Hanoi and the Holy See, diplomatic sources said on Wednesday.
The sources said papal envoy Archbishop Claudio Celli, was discussing ways around existing stumbling blocks, including Vietnam's refusal to accept a number of church appointments.
"We are still in the middle of the river and we are trying to land," said a church official, who declined to be identified.
Most of Vietnam's 75 million people are Budhhist, but its roughly seven million Catholic population is the second biggest in East Asia outside the Philippines.
Although church freedoms have improved since the late 1980s relations between the Vatican and Hanoi have alternated between lukewarm and frosty.
The Holy See reluctantly agreed in 1994 to allow Hanoi to review -- in effect to veto -- bishops' appointments.
The decision has resulted in a number of nominations being turned down.
The high-profile post occupied by the former archbishop of Ho Chi Minh City, Paul Nguyen Van Binh, has remained unfilled since his death in July 1995.

Archbishop Celli, who holds a position equivalent to deputy foreign minister, attended a mass for a small gathering of some 40 people in Hanoi on Wednesday in a building close to the city centre Franco-gothic Cathedral.
He was due to meet with government officials for further talks on Thursday before leaving Vietnam later in the week.
